title: Fix issues discovered by common python linters
description:
Fix some issues discovered by common python linters including:
* switch `None` comparisons to use `is` rather than `==`. Identity !=
equality, and I've spent 40+ hours before tracking down a subtle bug
caused by exactly this issue. Note that this may introduce a problem if
one of the scripts is depending on this behavior, in which case the
comparison should be changed to `True`/`False` rather than `None`.
* Use `except Exception:` as bare `except:` statements have been
discouraged for years. Ideally for some of these we'd examine if there
were specific exceptions that should be caught, but for now I simply
caught all. Again, this could introduce very subtle behavioral changes
under Python 2, but IIUC, that was all fixed in Python 3, so safe to
move to `except Exception:`.
* Use more idiomatic `if not x in y`--> `if x not in y`
* Use more idiomatic 2 blank lines. I only did this at the beginning,
until I realized how overwhelming this was going to be to apply, then I
stopped.
* Add a TODO where an undefined function name is called, so will fail
whenever that code is run.
* Add more idiomatic spacing around `:`. This is also only partially
cleaned up, as I gave up when I saw how `asn2wrs.py` was clearly
infatuated with the construct.
* Various other small cleanups, removed some trailing whitespace and
improper indentation that wasn't a multiple of 4, etc.

There is still _much_ to do, but I haven't been heavily involved with
this project before, so thought this was a sufficient amount to put up
and see what the feedback is.

Linters that I have enabled which highlighted some of these issues
include:
* `pylint`
* `flake8`
* `pycodestyle`

added 3 commits
  • c4bdb661...41e6b2f2 - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 68e58223 - Fix issues discovered by common python linters
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/346/diffs?diff_id=113186487&start_sha=c4bdb661eddfadd3f8a67ebfaa4d5a11bed464ca)

The calling function (`ip_checksum()`) is unused in this script, and has been since the initial commit 6 years ago in bed29af46db06f4bce00d8a4dab26317d4563dd3. It was broken in that initial commit as well, since `splitN()` wasn't defined. 

My suggested way to fix this is simply remove the entire `ip_checksum()` func altogether, given that it's been broken so long that it's clearly not being used.

Let me know how I should proceed.
@rknall can you address :point_up: ?

I'd like to merge this PR as it touches a bunch of code and this way we don't get too many merge conflicts... so I filed https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/16875 to track the above issue, and will simply leave the `TODO` comment in the merged code.

This is also a clear bug that needs fixing--it should be a `r`aw string so that the escape sequence in `\.c` is parsed properly. 

More details: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52335970/how-to-fix-string-deprecationwarning-invalid-escape-sequence-in-python

Agreed (after reading https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html#:~:text=The%20solution%20is%20to%20use,character%20string%20containing%20a%20newline.).

This code (which I wrote) happens to still to match the files I expected it to.  I sometimes add the r when they don't work as expected, but didn't really understand how python escaping otherwise competes with re escaping.

In general, most regex strings should use `r` (raw string, ie, don't parse in python)... it simplifies life for the code reader because you don't have to be like "okay, for the regex I need to escape this, and then for python I need to additionally escape this other thing"...
assigned to @crondaemon

I am happy with the changes to the scripts from tools that I have written, i.e.  check_dissector_urls.py, check_spelling.py, check_tfs.py and check_typed_item_calls.py.

The changes to other files look fine with me, but I'll give others a chance to comment before I properly try out and approve the change.

I have not used any of these tools before - will check them out.  I do inconsistently sometimes run my python code through autopep8.

Are the `check_ .py` scripts called automatically by the build or release processes?  
If not, should they be documented/mentioned in [README.developer](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/doc/README.developer) or [WSDG](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html/) and their use encouraged?

check_tfs.py and check_typed_item_calls.py are called by pipelines as part of the 'Code Checks + Clang warnings' build.  check_typed_item_calls.py has other command-line options that have found lots of issues, but they require careful examination.

I can draft something.  I don't think any of them (other than the 'safe' checks that are already done in the pipeline) should be recommended for every contributor to run, but I would be happy for someone to get use out of them and potentially help improve them.
The changes look good to me as well. Some of these scripts are pretty old (20 years in the case of ncp2222.py), so it's not surprising that they don't follow modern conventions.

commits_data.title: Fix issues discovered by common python linters
commits_data.message:
Fix issues discovered by common python linters

Fix some issues discovered by common python linters including:
* switch `None` comparisons to use `is` rather than `==`. Identity !=
equality, and I've spent 40+ hours before tracking down a subtle bug
caused by exactly this issue. Note that this may introduce a problem if
one of the scripts is depending on this behavior, in which case the
comparison should be changed to `True`/`False` rather than `None`.
* Use `except Exception:` as bare `except:` statements have been
discouraged for years. Ideally for some of these we'd examine if there
were specific exceptions that should be caught, but for now I simply
caught all. Again, this could introduce very subtle behavioral changes
under Python 2, but IIUC, that was all fixed in Python 3, so safe to
move to `except Exception:`.
* Use more idiomatic `if not x in y`--> `if x not in y`
* Use more idiomatic 2 blank lines. I only did this at the beginning,
until I realized how overwhelming this was going to be to apply, then I
stopped.
* Add a TODO where an undefined function name is called, so will fail
whenever that code is run.
* Add more idiomatic spacing around `:`. This is also only partially
cleaned up, as I gave up when I saw how `asn2wrs.py` was clearly
infatuated with the construct.
* Various other small cleanups, removed some trailing whitespace and
improper indentation that wasn't a multiple of 4, etc.

There is still _much_ to do, but I haven't been heavily involved with
this project before, so thought this was a sufficient amount to put up
and see what the feedback is.

Linters that I have enabled which highlighted some of these issues
include:
* `pylint`
* `flake8`
* `pycodestyle`
